attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between lan-a (opt1/vtnet1, 10.60.1.0/24, connected to node2) and lan-b (opt2/vtnet2, 10.60.2.0/24, connected to node3). Added pf rules that reject/refuse TCP port 23 in both directions between the two networks with logging enabled, while a general pass rule keeps other routed traffic (e.g. ICMP) flowing. Verified a telnet attempt from node2 to node3:23 is refused (RST/"Connection refused") and produces a filterlog entry on node1 showing block on vtnet1 from 10.60.1.2 to 10.60.2.2 port 23. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot markers + functional proof) on all three nodes, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms, confirmed each node's boot identity changed (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, Linux boot_id for node2/node3), and re-verified post-restart that routing, the telnet block, and the filter log all recovered correctly on every node.
